Criminal breach of trust.--Whoever, being in any manner entrusted with property, or with any dominion over property, dishonestly misappropriates or converts to his own use that property, or dishonestly uses or disposes of that property in violation of any direction of law prescribing the mode in which such trust is to be discharged, or of any legal contract, express or implied, which he has made touching the discharge of such trust, or wilfully suffers any other person so to do, commits
passed_precedents.judge_quote: The necessary ingredients of Section 405 IPC are detailed hereinbelow:- i) A person must be entrusted with a property or with dominion over any property. ii) The said person has to dishonestly misappropriate or convert to his own use that property or dishonestly use or dispose of that property in violation of any direction of law etc.

passed_precedents.text: A mere breach of trust does not automatically constitute a criminal offence; there must be proof of fraudulent or dishonest misappropriation to attract criminal liability.
passed_precedents.title: Sushree Snehal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 May, 2025
passed_precedents.quote: Every act of breach of trust may not result in a penal offence of criminal breach of trust unless there is evidence of manipulating act of fraudulent misappropriation.
passed_precedents.judge_quote: Every act of breach of trust may not result in a penal offence of criminal breach of trust unless there is evidence of manipulating act of fraudulent misappropriation. An act of breach of trust involves a civil wrong in respect of which the person may seek his remedy for damages in civil courts but, any breach of trust with a mens rea, gives rise to a criminal prosecution as well.

passed_precedents.text: Ordinary marital disagreements do not constitute an offence; only serious cruelty that endangers life, health or is linked to unlawful demands is punishable.
passed_precedents.title: Abuzar Ahmed vs The State Of Karnataka on 8 January, 2026
passed_precedents.quote: The law does not criminalize incompatibility, nor does it punish imperfect marriages. Section 498A of the IPC is not a panacea for all matrimonial ills. It is a targeted provision meant to address grave cruelty, conduct so wilful and pernicious so as to imperil life, limb or mental health or even harassment tethered to unlawful demands of dowry.
passed_precedents.judge_quote: The law does not criminalize incompatibility, nor does it punish imperfect marriages. Section 498A of the IPC is not a panacea for all matrimonial ills. It is a targeted provision meant to address grave cruelty, conduct so wilful and pernicious so as to imperil life, limb or mental health or even harassment tethered to unlawful demands of dowry.

passed_precedents.text: Judges should approach marital complaints with caution, look at the real‑life context, and examine the claims closely so that ordinary disagreements are not automatically treated as criminal cruelty.
passed_precedents.title: Abuzar Ahmed vs The State Of Karnataka on 8 January, 2026
passed_precedents.quote: Courts have to be extremely careful and cautious in dealing with complaints and must take pragmatic realities into consideration while dealing with matrimonial cases where the allegations have to be scrutinized with greater care and circumspection in order to prev
passed_precedents.judge_quote: Courts have to be extremely careful and cautious in dealing with complaints and must take pragmatic realities into consideration while dealing with matrimonial cases where the allegations have to be scrutinized with greater care and circumspection in order to prevent miscarriage of justice and abuse of process of law.

passed_precedents.text: To attract liability, the alleged conduct must be deliberate and intended to cause harm or misery to the woman.
passed_precedents.title: State vs Rishi Kumar And Ors. on 12 July, 2018
passed_precedents.quote: The use of the expression
passed_precedents.judge_quote: The cruelty, so as to attract penal provisions, contained in Section 468A State VS Rishi Kumar and Ors. FIR no. 388/16 PS - Sagarpur Page no. 33 of 76 of IPC , has necessarily to be a willful conduct which is of such a nature that it is likely to drive a woman to commit suicide or cause grievous injury or danger to her life or health. The use of the expression "willful" in the explanation to Section 498A of IPC indicates that the conduct attributed to the accused, in order to be culpable, needs to be deliberate, aimed at causing injury to the health of the woman or bringing misery to her.

passed_precedents.text: A presumption about demand or acceptance of illegal gratification can arise only if the prosecution proves basic facts; otherwise no presumption.
passed_precedents.title: V.Thambi Durai vs The State Rep By on 17 July, 2023
passed_precedents.quote: The presumption of fact with regard to the demand and acceptance or obtainment of an illegal gratification may be made by a court of law by way of an inference only when the foundational facts have been proved by relevant oral and documentary evidence and not in the absence thereof.
passed_precedents.judge_quote: The presumption of fact with regard to the demand and acceptance or obtainment of an illegal gratification may be made by a court of law by way of an inference only when the foundational facts have been proved by relevant oral and documentary evidence and not in the absence thereof.

passed_precedents.text: An imputation made in good faith for the protection of one's own or another's interest or for the public good is exempt from defamation under the Ninth Exception.
passed_precedents.title: S. Bangarappa vs Ganesh Narayan Hegade And Others on 16 June, 1992
passed_precedents.quote: Ninth Exception - Imputation made in good faith by person for protection of his or other's interests : It is not defamation to make an imputation on the character of another provided that the imputation be made in good faith for protection of the interest of the person making it, or of any other person, or for the public good.
passed_precedents.judge_quote: Explanation 9 to S. 499 , IPC absolves a person from conviction in case the imputation made is in good faith and it reads thus : "Ninth Exception - Imputation made in good faith by person for protection of his or other's interests : It is not defamation to make an imputation on the character of another provided that the imputation be made in good faith for protection of the interest of the person making it, or of any other person, or for the public good."

passed_precedents.text: To establish defamation under IPC, the prosecution must prove that the accused intended or knew or had reason to believe that the imputation would harm the complainant's reputation; lack of such mens rea defeats the offence.
passed_precedents.title: Arundhati Sapru vs Yash Mehra on 12 November, 2013
passed_precedents.quote: Thus, it is clear that the mens rea to cause harm is the most essential sine qua non for an offence under section 499 IPC.
passed_precedents.judge_quote: Thus, it is clear that the mens rea to cause harm is the most essential sine qua non for an offence under section 499 IPC. To constitute "defamation" under Section 499 of the IPC, there must be an imputation and such imputation must have been made with intention of harming or knowing or having reason to believe that it will harm the reputation of the person about whom it is made.

passed_precedents.text: To be convicted of criminal defamation, the accused must have intended to harm the plaintiff’s reputation; without that intent, there is no guilt.
passed_precedents.title: Standard Chartered Bank vs Vinay Kumar Sood & Ors. on 6 February, 2009
passed_precedents.quote: For inviting the provisions contained in Section 499 / 500 IPC which are penal in nature, a Magistrate has to consider if the requirement of mens rea which is a mandate for a criminal defamation punishable under Section 500 IPC was fulfilled. If mens rea or criminal intention is lacking or is missing in the act of the accused, he cannot be held guilty for an offence of defamation within the meaning of Section 499 IPC.
passed_precedents.judge_quote: Thus, it is clear that intention to cause harm is the most essential sine qua non for an offence under Section 499 IPC. An offence punishable under Section 500 IPC requires blameworthy mind and is not a statutory offence requiring no mens rea.

passed_precedents.text: Mens rea (intent to harm) is a necessary element for defamation under IPC.

passed_precedents.text: A good‑faith accusation made to someone with lawful authority over the accused is exempt from defamation liability.
passed_precedents.title: P. Sharma vs P.S. Popli And Anr. on 9 November, 2001
passed_precedents.quote: Exception 8 to Section 499 clearly indicates that it is not a defamation to prefer in good faith an accusation against any person to any of those who have lawful authority over that person with regard to the subject matter of accusation.
passed_precedents.judge_quote: Exception 8 provides that it is 'not' defamation to prefer, in good faith an accusation against any person to any of those who has lawful authority over that person, with respect to the subject matter of accusation. The illustration to this Exception makes it absolutely clear. It reads:- Illustration:-- If A in good faith accuses Z before a Magistrate; if A in good faith complains of the conduct of Z, a servant, to Z,s master; if A in good faith complains of the conduct of Z, a child, to Z's father - is within this exception.

passed_precedents.quote: For proceeding against an accused for the commission of the offence of cheating u/Sec. 420 IPC , the dishonest inducement must be shown to have caused delivery of property to any person, or to have brought about the making, alteration, destruction of a valuable security even a part thereof, or of anything that is signed Page No. 23 of 35 and sealed and is capable of being converted into a valuable security.
passed_precedents.judge_quote: For proceeding against an accused for the commission of the offence of cheating u/Sec. 420 IPC , the dishonest inducement must be shown to have caused delivery of property to any person, or to have brought about the making, alteration, destruction of a valuable security even a part thereof, or of anything that is signed Page No. 23 of 35 and sealed and is capable of being converted into a valuable security.

passed_precedents.judge_quote: Section 415 in The Indian Penal Code 415. Cheating.--Whoever, by deceiving any person, fraudulently or dishonestly induces the person so deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to consent that any person shall retain any property, or intentionally induces the person so deceived to do or omit to do anything which he would not do or omit if he were not so deceived, and which act or omission causes or is likely to cause damage or harm to that person in body, mind, reputation or property, is said to "cheat".

passed_precedents.text: A formal closure of the trading window is not required for compliance with insider‑trading rules if there is no actual trading or misuse of unpublished price‑sensitive information.
passed_precedents.title: Piramal Enterprises Limited vs Sebi on 15 May, 2019
passed_precedents.quote: Thus, even though, no announcement was made for closure of the trading window, we find that PEL ensured compliance in pith and substance of the Model Code of PEL and the PIT Regulations including the Model Code.
passed_precedents.judge_quote: The purpose of closing the trading window is for a salutary purpose. It is to ensure that trading is restricted during the period in question and pre-clearance requests can only be sanctioned as per the existing Model Code of PEL. In the given circumstances, even though the trading window was not closed, there was no trading of the scrips by any of the designated employees of the PEL nor any pre-clearance requests were received by PEL. Thus, even though, no announcement was made for closure of the trading window, we find that PEL ensured compliance in pith and substance of the Model Code of PEL and the PIT Regulations including the Model Code. We further find that UPSI at all times was preserved and there was no misuse of UPSI.

passed_precedents.text: An insider is someone who is presently or formerly linked to the firm, or is treated as linked, and thus is anticipated to acquire confidential price‑sensitive data about the company’s securities, or who actually acquires that data.
passed_precedents.title: In Re: Shri D.S. Pendse And Ors.; In Re: ... vs Unknown on 11 January, 2008
passed_precedents.quote: 'insider' means any person who, is or was connected with the company or is deemed to have connected with the company, and who is reasonably expected to have access, by virtue of such connection, to unpublished price sensitive information in respect of securities of the company, or who has received or has received or has had access to such unpublished price sensitive information.
passed_precedents.judge_quote: The term "insider" is defined under Regulation 2(e) of the Insider Regulations. It reads as under- "'insider' means any person who, is or was connected with the company or is deemed to have connected with the company, and who is reasonably expected to have access, by virtue of such connection, to unpublished price sensitive information in respect of securities of the company, or who has received or has received or has had access to such unpublished price sensitive information."

passed_precedents.text: The regulations prohibit an insider from dealing, communicating, or counseling others to deal in securities based on unpublished price sensitive information.
passed_precedents.title: In Re: Shri D.S. Pendse And Ors.; In Re: ... vs Unknown on 11 January, 2008
passed_precedents.quote: No insider shall - i. either on his own behalf, or on behalf of any other person, deal in securities of a company listed on any stock exchange on the basis of any unpublished price sensitive information; ii. or (ii) communicate any unpublished price sensitive information to any person, with or without his request for such information, except as required in the ordinary course of business or under any law; iii. or (iii) counsel or procure any other person to deal in securities of any company on the basis of unpublished price sensitive information.
passed_precedents.judge_quote: Regulation 3 of the Insider Regulations reads as under- 3. Prohibition on dealing, communication or counseling on matters relating to insider trading - No insider shall - i. either on his own behalf, or on behalf of any other person, deal in securities of a company listed on any stock exchange on the basis of any unpublished price sensitive information; ii. or (ii) communicate any unpublished price sensitive information to any person, with or without his request for such information, except as required in the ordinary course of business or under any law; iii. or (iii) counsel or procure any other person to deal in securities of any company on the basis of unpublished price sensitive information.
